no_tumor.title: No Tumor Detected
no_tumor.description: The brain MRI was classified by the AI model as showing no tumor pattern in the categories used by this project.
risk_factors: No tumor-specific risk factors are applicable when no tumor is detected.
MRI interpretation should still be confirmed by a qualified healthcare professional when clinically indicated.
treatment: No tumor-specific treatment is indicated by this AI prediction alone.
If symptoms or clinical concerns are present, appropriate medical evaluation should be sought.

glioma.title: Glioma
glioma.description: Gliomas are tumors that arise from glial cells or related cells in the central nervous system. They can vary widely in their biological behavior and grade.
risk_factors: Most gliomas do not have a clearly identifiable cause.
Certain inherited genetic conditions can increase the risk of developing gliomas.
Previous exposure to ionizing radiation is an established risk factor in some cases.
Age and certain genetic or molecular changes can influence the likelihood and characteristics of gliomas.
treatment: Treatment depends on the tumor type, grade, molecular characteristics, location, size, and the person's overall clinical situation.
Possible treatment approaches include surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or combinations of these approaches.
Some patients may also undergo monitoring or additional specialized treatment depending on the tumor characteristics.

meningioma.title: Meningioma
meningioma.description: Meningiomas are tumors that arise from the meninges, the protective membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord. Many meningiomas are slow-growing.
risk_factors: Increasing age is associated with a higher likelihood of meningioma.
Certain genetic conditions can increase risk.
Previous exposure to ionizing radiation, particularly to the head, is an established risk factor.
Hormonal and genetic factors may also have a role in some meningiomas.
treatment: Some small or slow-growing meningiomas may be monitored with regular imaging.
Surgery may be considered when the tumor causes symptoms, grows, or can be safely removed.
Radiation therapy or other specialized treatments may be considered in selected cases.
The appropriate approach depends on tumor location, size, growth, symptoms, and other clinical factors.

pituitary.title: Pituitary Tumor
pituitary.description: Pituitary tumors develop in or around the pituitary gland. Many are benign and some can affect hormone production or nearby structures.
risk_factors: The exact cause of most pituitary tumors is not known.
Some inherited genetic syndromes can increase the risk of pituitary tumors.
Hormonal and genetic factors may influence certain pituitary tumors.
treatment: Treatment depends on the tumor type, size, hormone activity, symptoms, and effect on nearby structures.
Some pituitary tumors can be monitored without immediate treatment.
Medication may be used for certain hormone-producing pituitary tumors.
Surgery or radiation therapy may be considered in selected cases.

disclaimer: This information is provided for educational purposes only. The AI model's prediction is not a medical diagnosis and should not be used by itself to determine treatment or medical decisions.
